children: Occidental Petroleum
is heading into third-quarter earnings with a much stronger commodity-price backdrop, after the company disclosed that its
average realized oil price jumped roughly 33% year over year
during a quarter shaped by supply disruptions tied to the U.S.-Iran war.
Occidental said its worldwide average realized oil price rose to
$85.91 per barrel in Q3
, up from $64.78 a year earlier.
Natural gas liquids pricing also improved sharply, climbing to
$24.63 per barrel from $19.60
, while worldwide realized natural gas prices edged up to
$1.69 per Mcf from $1.57
Those price gains should provide a meaningful earnings tailwind.
But the quarter was not entirely clean.
Occidental also said it temporarily curtailed production at some of its U.S. Gulf facilities because of a
third-party gas pipeline constraint and maintenance activity
That introduces an offsetting operational issue: higher commodity prices improve revenue per barrel, but lower production can limit how much of that benefit reaches the bottom line.
The company also disclosed that crude-oil collar settlements reduced operating cash flow before working capital by
$94 million
in the quarter.
Shares rose about
0.8% Tuesday
following the filing.
Investor Takeaway
I think the setup for Occidental is straightforward:
pricing is materially better, but investors still need to see how much production disruption offsets that benefit
A realized oil price near $86 per barrel is a major improvement from last year and should support cash generation, especially if operating costs remain controlled.
At the same time, temporary Gulf curtailments and the $94 million hedge-related cash-flow hit mean the quarter may not fully reflect the strength of the commodity environment.
For investors, the key things to watch are
production volumes, realized oil prices, free cash flow, Gulf restoration timelines and debt reduction

If Occidental can pair these higher prices with stable production, the earnings leverage could be substantial. If operational constraints persist, however, some of that upside may remain trapped in the commodity backdrop rather than flowing through to results.

title: Occidental Gets Major Price Boost Ahead of Q3
